A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XBT research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-modal retrieval experiments, ablations, continual-learning results, computational measurements, and appendix classification experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an image-only pretraining control in Table 4.

M1.justification: The proposed text-pretrained projection, Gaussian noise injection, contrastive objectives, LoRA, visual prompts, and projection layer-normalization tuning remain unchanged. Image-only pretraining appears as an experimental control, without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The reported training and evaluation coverage is retained, including nocaps, Flickr, COCO, CC3M, and the three ImageNet classification benchmarks. Flickr-31K and COCO-35K are renamed Large-Flickr and Large-COCO with identical sample counts. Continual-learning evaluation already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated image-only pretraining alternative to the comparison in Table 4. Full-tune, LoRA-only, Base, and the original CLIP/BLIP comparators remain present in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The new Table 4 control replaces text pretraining with image pretraining at the same reported scale, evaluated on nocaps with B32 as the old model and L14 as the new model. Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds an ablation testing whether projection pretraining with images performs as well as pretraining with text. v1 discussed this comparison only as future research. Existing noise, data-scale, alternative-training-data, continual-learning, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional ablation follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds image-only results of 45.32 and 76.92 for text-to-image retrieval, and 74.02 and 92.35 for image-to-text retrieval, below the retained text-pretraining baseline entries. All previously reported numerical table values remain unchanged, including the relocated appendix results.

T1.justification: The compatibility constraints and relaxed criterion in Equations 1–2, objectives and projection definitions in Equations 3–6, and text/image distribution hypothesis are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing XBT, enabling backfill-free cross-modal retrieval through a text-pretrained projection, and using parameter-efficient training while preserving the original new model's capabilities.

C2.justification: v1's speculative discussion of image-only pretraining is replaced by an interpretation that the new control supports text pretraining's superiority and efficiency. v2 also removes Section 5's explicit limitation concerning training-data quality, diversity, and representational richness.

D1.justification: The training recipe from v1 Appendix A.2 moves into v2 Section 4.1 with unchanged hardware, batch sizes, optimizer settings, augmentation, prompts, and checkpoint identifiers. Projection architecture, LoRA settings, computational measurements, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kim et al. (2021), 'How to adapt your large-scale vision-and-language model,' to the introduction's parameter-efficient training citations. The other cited works and positioning relative to backward-compatible, continual, and transfer learning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose remains unchanged. The training recipe and continual-learning discussion move into the main text, while BLIP evaluation moves to the supplement. Dataset names, some headings, and author information change, and the limitations and speculative image-only discussion are removed.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from one column to two. Figures 1–2 are rearranged vertically, Figure 3 is simplified, and the separate Flickr/COCO tables are merged. Continual-learning and BLIP tables move between the main text and supplement, and Table 4 gains a row.

improvement.justification: The new matched-scale image-only control directly tests a central design choice that v1 left for future research, providing limited empirical support for choosing text pretraining. Existing results and reproducibility information are preserved. Removing the explicit data-quality limitation weakens qualification, but the added experimental evidence provides a modest overall benefit.
